title: The Four Bedrock Laws
summary: Work through The Four Bedrock Laws.

blocks.md: This lesson follows **The Four Bedrock Laws** in *The Causal Boundary* (Vol IV).

blocks.source: Vol IV, The Causal Boundary, § The Four Bedrock Laws
blocks.md: Every check on the permission path answers to constraints that neither a learned policy nor a software supervisor can negotiate away. Whether the warehouse machine is braking for a coworker in an aisle, pressing a spring-latched cage door, or carrying an unmodeled payload, it must respect the mechanical limits of its plant, adapt to dynamic environments altered by its own motion, and arbitrate between speculative model outputs and physically safe actuation. Four bedrock laws organize these engineering responsibilities, each anchoring a major part of this book:

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Proposal boundary matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: A learned model may only propose; an independent permission path with bounded latency, which the model cannot delay or corrupt, alone admits an action after checking fresh evidence, the stopping envelope, and a feasible fallback, and it acts on its own when the proposer stalls.

questions.q: The section **The Four Bedrock Laws** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A learned model may only propose; an independent permission path with bounded latency, which the model cannot delay or corrupt, alone admits an action after checking fresh evidence, the stopping envelope, and a feasible fallback, and it acts on its own when the proposer stalls.

Embodied operation divides by the margin it spends (stopping clearance for mass-dominated mobility, force and deformation for contact-dominated manipulation, heat and supply for energy- and thermal-dominated operation), and one task can cross all three.
Each chapter contributes one machine-checkable record of an assumption with its evidence, producer, consumers, and invalidating conditions, and the chain of records meets at the permission decision.

The causal boundary is the interface where an admitted digital command begins to drive current, force, or flow in the plant; upstream a tensor is a proposal that can be discarded for free, and downstream changing the command costs physical work against inertia over finite time.
